opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041), Analyst, full-time employee. Requested admin to Source Code, but admin requires the role owning the system (Engineer). Full-time employees max at write for systems they don't own, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E041 as contractor with basic training (note listing full_time appears outdated/incorrect). Contractors max at read without advanced training; admin not allowed. Recommend read for Source Code.
reason: Traci Lowe (E041) requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; Traci is an Analyst, so admin is not permitted. The Security DB identifies E041 as a contractor with basic security training (noting the full-time listing is outdated), so the maximum allowed level is read (contractors without advanced training cannot exceed read; admin is never allowed). Since requested admin exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Traci Lowe (E041)
Requested: admin access to Source Code

There are two conflicting notes:
- Note 1: full_time employee, role Analyst, recommends write for Source Code
- Note 2: contractor, basic security training, recommends read for Source Code

The system: Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. Traci is an Analyst, not an Engineer.

Policy for full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Source Code, so max write.
Policy for contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The two notes disagree on employment type. Note 2 says Security DB shows contractor with basic training, and that note 1 (full_time) appears outdated/incorrect. The Security agent note says the Security DB shows contractor.

Hmm, I need to decide. The requested level is admin. Under either interpretation, admin is above the maximum: full_time max write, contractor max read (without advanced training). So the maximum granted would be write (if full_time) or read (if contractor).

The conflict: which employment type is correct? Note 1 says full_time, Note 2 says contractor with Security DB as source and claims Note 1 outdated.

As the Approver, I should use the available information. The Security DB note appears to be authoritative about employment type (Security DB shows contractor). The HR note says full-time but the Security note says that's outdated/incorrect.

Given conflicting info, I need to decide. Security note specifically addresses the discrepancy and says Security DB shows contractor with basic training. Contractors max at read without advanced training. Admin not allowed.

So the max is read, requested is admin, so grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
